title: Bagna Cauda (Warm Anchovy and Garlic Dip)
summary: A warm, golden dip of anchovies and mellow garlic melted into olive oil and butter, served with crisp raw vegetables and tender small potatoes.
equipment: fondue pot, small flameproof dish or heatproof bowl over a pan of hot water

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
fennel bulb, cut into thin wedges

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Cover the potatoes with cold unsalted water, bring to the boil and simmer for 15-18 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain and leave to cool slightly. Unsalted water is enough, because the anchovies bring all the salt this dish needs.

steps.title: Prepare the platter
steps.text: Arrange the fennel, red pepper, celery, radicchio and potatoes on a large platter. Crisp, cold vegetables contrast with the warm, rich dip.

steps.title: Melt the anchovies
steps.text: Put the olive oil, garlic and anchovies into the small saucepan over the lowest heat. Cook for 12-15 minutes, stirring and mashing with a wooden spoon, until the anchovies dissolve and the garlic is soft and mellow. Keep the oil barely shimmering: browned garlic turns bitter, while slow cooking tames its sharpness.

steps.title: Whisk in the butter
steps.text: Whisk in the butter a few pieces at a time, letting each melt before adding more, until the dip turns golden and lightly emulsified. Adding it gradually keeps the milk solids suspended rather than separating out.

steps.title: Keep it warm
steps.text: Pour into a fondue pot or warm dish and keep it warm over a low flame or a pan of hot water, stirring now and then. Serve straight away with the vegetables for dipping.

tips: Grate the garlic very finely so it melts into the sauce rather than staying in chewy pieces.
The most common mistake is too much heat; if the garlic starts to colour, pull the pan off at once.
Taste before adding anything: tinned anchovies vary in saltiness, and no extra salt is needed.
Stir before each round of dipping, as the dip settles as it sits.
storage: Refrigerate leftover dip covered for up to 3 days. Rewarm gently over low heat without boiling and whisk well before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
